dedupe_keys.name: new zealand estuaries spatial database department of conservation

description: The New Zealand estuaries spatial database of the Department of Conservation is an interactive map for exploring data on estuaries, rivers, river catchments and the marine environment, with drop-down menus and tick boxes to combine layers, such as seagrass extent with coastal turbidity, or wetlands and protected areas in vulnerable catchments. The page describes each layer and its source: vulnerable catchments and land cover, estuary eutrophication and river water quality, the national mangroves and seagrass database, public inanga spawning records, ecological districts and regions, the NIWA estuary environment classification, the Ministry for the Environment coastal hydrosystem classification, marine habitats of the territorial sea, current (2013) and historical wetland extent from Manaaki Whenua mapped at 1:50,000, mean high water springs, a bathymetry compiled from LINZ nautical charts, and management areas such as public conservation land, type 2 marine protected areas that also protect submarine cables and pipelines, and council boundaries. Access to the map is free online; no licence is stated on the page read, and sources are credited per layer. Caveats: layers come from different agencies and dates, and some, like the spawning records, rely on public observations that may be incomplete. Coverage is New Zealand. It supports coastal flood and nature-based adaptation analysis around estuaries, and siting of coastal infrastructure and cables; related records are the Korean inland wetland data and the Danish coastal data (Kystdata).
